definition: An organic compound formed when an alcohol reacts with a carboxylic acid, releasing water. Members carry the -COO- functional group; small ones are volatile with distinctive smells.
msAccepts: formed from an alcohol and a carboxylic acid
water is eliminated when it forms
msAvoids: calling it an alcohol or an acid
omitting one of the two parent families
writing -COOH as the ester group

definition: The atom arrangement that gives an organic family its characteristic reactions. The ester group is -COO-: a carbon double-bonded to one oxygen and single-bonded to another.
msAccepts: the reactive arrangement determining chemical properties
msAvoids: omitting that it dictates reactions
giving -COOH (the acid group) for esters

definition: The family of weak organic acids carrying -COOH; one of the two parents of every ester. Made by oxidising the corresponding alcohol.
msAccepts: weak organic acid formed from alcohol oxidation
reacts with an alcohol to give an ester
msAvoids: confusing the acid's -COOH with the ester's -COO-
calling it the ester's product rather than parent

definition: The family of organic compounds carrying the hydroxyl group -OH; the other parent of every ester, naming the alkyl part of the ester's name.
msAccepts: reacts with a carboxylic acid to give an ester
provides the alkyl part of the ester name
msAvoids: omitting the -OH group
confusing with the alkane family

definition: The reaction of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid to form an ester and water, run over a concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst with heat. Reversible.
msAccepts: alcohol plus carboxylic acid gives ester plus water
msAvoids: omitting the catalyst or the heat
writing the catalyst into the equation
omitting water as the second product

definition: A reaction in which two molecules join together while a small molecule, here water, is released. Esterification is the chapter's example.
msAccepts: two molecules join with loss of a small molecule
water released as the molecules join
msAvoids: omitting the small-molecule loss
confusing with addition, where nothing is expelled

definition: A substance that speeds a reaction without being consumed. Concentrated sulfuric acid catalyses esterification, so it is named in the conditions but never written into the equation.
msAccepts: not consumed / unchanged at the end
msAvoids: describing it as used up
balancing it into the equation
omitting it from the conditions

definition: Pure, water-free ethanoic acid. Used in ester synthesis so no water is added to the equilibrium mixture, protecting the ester yield.
msAccepts: used to keep water out of the equilibrium
msAvoids: calling it dilute acid
omitting why purity protects the yield

definition: A reaction running in both directions at once, reaching a position of equilibrium. Esterification is reversible, so water added to the mixture shifts the position left and lowers the ester yield.
msAccepts: added water shifts the position left, reducing ester
msAvoids: treating the yield as fixed
saying the equilibrium 'wants' anything (teleology)
omitting the shift direction

definition: The ester CH3COOCH2CH3, made from ethanol and ethanoic acid over an acid catalyst; the chapter's representative ester and a nail-polish solvent.
msAccepts: ester of ethanol and ethanoic acid
msAvoids: writing CH3COOC2H5's parents the wrong way round
omitting a formula level when drawing is asked
calling it ethyl acetic

definition: The unambiguous condensed formula showing atom arrangement without every bond drawn, such as CH3COOCH2CH3 for ethyl ethanoate.
msAvoids: confusing with the molecular formula C4H8O2
drawing every bond when condensed is asked

definition: The drawing that shows every bond explicitly, including the C=O and C-O of the ester group. Required when a question says 'displayed'.
msAvoids: giving the condensed formula instead
omitting the double-bonded oxygen
omitting hydrogens on carbon

definition: The fragment of an ester that came from the alcohol, named by the 'yl' word: methyl, ethyl, propyl, butyl. It bonds through its spare oxygen to the alkanoate part.
msAccepts: the 'yl' part names the alcohol it came from
methyl means methanol was the parent
msAvoids: reading the 'yl' word as the acid
omitting the oxygen link between the fragments

definition: The fragment of an ester that came from the carboxylic acid, named by the 'oate' word and always containing the C=O carbon: methanoate, ethanoate, propanoate, butanoate.
msAccepts: the 'oate' part names the carboxylic acid
the C=O carbon is in the alkanoate part
ethanoate means ethanoic acid was the parent
msAvoids: reading the 'oate' word as the alcohol
miscounting carbons by excluding the carbonyl carbon

definition: Turns to vapour easily. Volatility is why esters work as flavourings and perfumes: the molecules leave the liquid and carry their smells through the air.
msAccepts: links volatility to the smell reaching the nose
msAvoids: defining it as flammable or unstable
naming the use without the volatility link

definition: The intermolecular force between an O-H group and water. Alcohols and carboxylic acids hydrogen-bond and dissolve; esters have no O-H and so hardly dissolve.
msAccepts: attraction between O-H and water molecules
explains solubility of small alcohols and acids
esters lack O-H so form weak interactions with water
msAvoids: calling it a covalent bond
claiming esters dissolve because they contain oxygen

definition: The liquid something dissolves in. Small esters such as ethyl ethanoate are used as solvents, for example in nail polish and nail polish remover.
msAccepts: ethyl ethanoate as a solvent in nail polish
msAvoids: confusing with the solute
omitting the nail-polish example when asked for a use

definition: The 0.5 mol/dm3 solution the ester mixture is poured into after cooling; it reacts with the excess acid (effervescence) so the ester's smell is no longer masked.
msAccepts: reacts with / neutralises the excess acid
so the ester can be smelled better
msAvoids: saying it catalyses the esterification
saying it reacts with the ester
omitting the smell-masking reason
